description:
A room as its index reads it (0.79.0). A room keeps an index by saving one convention file at
        `.hashn/index.md`: `convention: convention`, `dimensions` with members written inside members, and
        `file_tree: <dimension>` naming the dimension whose members are the room's folders. Returns each folder the
        index names (its parents, its children, its description, the files sitting in it, of any type; a folder
        with no files exists only here), the files in folders the index does not name (not wrong: their author's
        own), and what the index lost against its version before. In query_index the file-tree dimension is a
        column: the folder a file sits in gives its value, and a header that names another member is flagged in
        `issues`. Read only: nothing is refused, and who may read or write a room is unchanged. A room without an
        index returns `index: null` and how to keep one. 0.80.0: `rules` lists the room's rule files. A rule file is
        `<folder>/.hashn/rules.md` (at the top of the room: `.hashn/rules.md`) with `checks`, the vocabulary a
        convention has; they apply to every file in that folder and beneath, whatever its convention (`applies_to`
        narrows to some), and a file that breaks one is flagged in `issues` and on save, never refused. 0.82.0:
        for members, `writers` lists the folders the owner shared for writing (share_folder) and with whom; the
        index and rule files themselves are the owner's to write unless their `.hashn` folder is shared. 0.83.0:
        a folder kept from you by a reader list is not in your tree (its files, its rule file); `readers` lists the
        reader lists on the folders you read. 0.84.0, the composite index: a convention file of
        the same form at `<folder>/.hashn/index.md` (a sub index) continues the tree beneath the member that folder is;
        `index.sub_indexes` lists them (path, the member each continues, what is not read), `folders` is the one
        tree, and you see the sub indexes of the folders you read.
